submitted.rationale: Index 17 (Ca 0.327, Mn 0.673; the CaMn2O4 composition) gave the highest photocurrent measured, 1.59 µA. MEGNet predicts CaMn2O4 has a 2.54 eV band gap, which the 3.22 eV light can excite. The other two measurements came from either side of it: Ca 0.407 gave 0.66 µA and Ca 0.254 gave 0. So the best result is near the CaMn2O4 composition.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.66 µA, lower than index 17, even though Ca2Mn3O8 has a predicted 2.69 eV gap.
Measured 0 A. On the Mn-rich side the Ca-Mn phases are predicted to be near-metallic (for example CaMn5O7 at 0.15 eV).
Not measured. Predicted to be near-metallic (0.19 and 0.29 eV), and photocurrent fell as Ca increased from 0.33 to 0.41.

consultations.verdict: Support: MEGNet HSE gaps show CaMn2O4 (Ca 0.333) 2.54 eV and Ca2Mn3O8 (Ca 0.4) 2.69 eV — semiconducting and below the 3.22 eV photon energy — whereas CaMnO3 (0.19 eV) and CaMn7O12 (0.82 eV) are near-metallic. Index 17 (Ca 0.327) sits at CaMn2O4 composition.

Support (relative): Ca3Mn2O7 is predicted near-metallic (0.29 eV) and CaMn4O8 1.10 eV, so the Ca-rich and Mn-rich neighbours look worse than Ca2Mn3O8 (2.69 eV, earlier receipt), which sits at index 3's composition (Ca 0.407).

Mixed: CaMn5O7 (Ca 0.167) predicted near-metallic (0.15 eV), which argues against the very Mn-rich end. But measured photocurrent rose 2.4x going from Ca 0.41 to 0.33, and the GP favours the unexplored Mn-rich region. Index 21 (Ca 0.254) tests whether the trend continues past CaMn2O4 without going all the way to the metallic end. Index 17 is already secured as a fallback.
